newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen sees 1997 deals over US$600 mln.
newsitem.headline: Loewen sees 1997 deals over US$600 mln.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc said Thursday it expects to make US$600 million to US$700 million in acquisitions next year.
"We are quite comfortable believing we will be in the US$600 million to US$700 million range," chairman Ray Loewen told analysts in a telephone conference call.
Loewen through September was involved in deals to buy cemeteries and funeral homes worth US$1.3 billion.
Although he projected a decrease in acquisitions for next year, Loewen said the company was traditionally conservative in this regard and had exceeded its expectations in the past.

Loewen's standing among independent funeral home and cemetery owners who might sell to it is strong. Its "political positioning" in the industry has never been better, Loewen said, describing this as a sign of support for its effort to remain independent.
"Every dollar of acquisitions we think of as a vote," he said. Loewen is fighting a US$2.9 billion hostile takeover bid from Service Corp International.
So far this year about half the acquisitions have been for funeral homes and half for cemeteries.

The projected return on investment for the US$797 million in deals is more than 16 percent, the company said. Of that, US$400 million were so-called "mom and pop" operators on which the return on investment is expected to average 19 percent.
Loewen said the US$150 million in acquisitions signed since the Service bid was launched were done at "normal prices," apparently meaning there has be no rapid escalation.
The company said Service's exchange offer was still awaiting clearance by the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Commenting on earnings, Loewen said its gross margins for funeral homes fell in the third quarter to 38.5 percent from 40 percent the prior year.
The company attributed this partly to a drop in case volumes of about three percent on a same store basis in the quarter and about 2.3 percent year to date.

Loewen said it was pleased with this because industrywide the decline has ranged from three to 13 percent. The drop in case volume caused about one percentage point of the gross margin decline. Loewen said the margin fall was also due to its aggressive acquisition program.

Gross margins for its cemetery business rose to 34.3 percent in the quarter from 28.4 percent the prior year. But Loewen said this was not sustainable long term and suggested 32 percent was a more reasonable expectation.
Loewen said the 1996 amount had exceeded the company's expectations.
"There's no way we would project the same level in 1997," Loewen said.
Of that US$1.3 billion, US$535 million were in two structured transactions with Blackstone Capital Partners. Those deals should be considered "one time events" he said.
Excluding those deals, the funeral home operator signed or closed US$797 milion in acquisitions so far this year. Loewen said about US$200 million of that would be carried over and closed in 1997.
